blocks.content: Landscape is a function of structure, process, and stage.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Geographical Cycle of Erosion was formulated by William Morris Davis in 1899 to explain landform evolution.
The Youthful Stage is dominated by steep gradients, high kinetic energy, active vertical downcutting, V-shaped valleys, gorges, and waterfalls.
The Mature Stage shifts emphasis to lateral erosion, valley widening, floodplains, and maximum relief diversity.
The Old Age (Senile) Stage features low gradient, heavy deposition, oxbow lakes, broad floodplains, and ultimate base-level reduction.
The ultimate result of the Davisian cycle is a featureless plain termed a 'Peneplain' studded with resistant residual hills called 'Monadnocks'.
Davisian Triad: Frequently asked in UPSC GS-I & Geography Optional—'Structure, Process, and Stage' govern landscape evolution.
Stage Identification: Associate Gorges/Waterfalls with Youth Stage, Meanders/Oxbow Lakes with Mature Stage, and Peneplains/Monadnocks with Old Age Stage.
Base Level Concept: Understand that rivers cannot erode lower than grand base level (sea level).
